tickets.summary: K-3401 NDE bearing vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s in six weeks with growing 1x/sidebands. Still below alarm but not plateaued, it threatens the sole export train; a trip would recycle the platform and cut production within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating-equipment specialist to diagnose; engineer to approve correction based on findings and continue daily trending. Obtain source-required attention today. Check current vibration and export status. Inspect NDE bearing and 1x spectrum.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The non-drive-end vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s over six weeks and has not plateaued, supporting strong progression toward loss of compressor function. It remained below alarm at the observation; a trip or present loss of export function is not established. The later cladding observation concerns a different mechanism.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If this sole gas-export compressor train trips, the platform goes to recycle and production is cut within an hour; no spare or workaround is identified. This is the consequence of a potential trip, not an observed trip.

tickets.summary: PSV-1310 hisses at its outlet with hydrocarbon smell below set pressure; guidance treats suspected passing as protection impairment. Relief capability is untested, leaving V-1201 overpressure protection in doubt.
tickets.recommended_action: Relief engineer: inspect tailpipe/PSV, set regulatory disposition and approve repair as indicated. Check PSV impairment/deviation register. Witness PSV tightness and certified pop tests. Check current PSV status and controls. Confirm tailpipe leak source and gas exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Audible hissing and a hydrocarbon smell below set pressure indicate an active concern, but the source is unconfirmed and no relief-capability test establishes loss of overpressure protection.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If this nonredundant relief valve cannot protect V-1201 from overpressure, a severe pressure-boundary and personnel hazard is credible; the observed hiss is not evidence that this consequence has occurred.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first firewater test start, then started after ~8 s cranking; batteries read 22.8 V at rest and running pressure was rated. Fire protection is degraded; FW-8101's later 9.2/11 barg with flow unmeasured leaves backup capacity unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Firewater engineer to assess fire cover and approve operating/repair disposition; inspect starter, repair cause. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Check battery/charger and air under cranking. Test FW-8101 flow/pressure against criteria. Witness first-start and rated pressure/flow.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: FW-8102's required firewater start function failed on the first weekly-test attempt. It started on the second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking and then achieved rated discharge pressure; that success does not erase the failed start or establish reliable restoration. Battery and starting-air faults recur, but the cause of this attempt is unconfirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this pump to start on demand degrades firewater protection. FW-8101 is the designated N+1 partner, but its later test recorded 9.2 barg against 11 barg design with flow unmeasured; its delivery capability cannot yet be credited or declared lost. The source identifies production shutdown if both pumps are unavailable, without establishing that both are unavailable.

tickets.summary: At window 2 by the low-point drain, PL-1002 has 6.2 mm wall against a 7.4 mm minimum beneath wet insulation; adjacent windows pass, but containment loss could expose personnel and interrupt hydrocarbon transfer.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to assess operating/repair disposition and approve correction of under-minimum wall. Check current service, pressure and leakage. Map UT extent beneath wet insulation. Check personnel exposure at flowline.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is containment by the PL-1002 production flowline. Wet insulation, heavy scaling and a local wall reading below the stated minimum indicate advanced damage and a strong precursor to containment loss. The UT survey does not establish that the pipe has leaked or lost containment.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of containment on a nonredundant hydrocarbon flowline described as live at full wellhead pressure presents a credible severe release and personnel-exposure hazard and could interrupt transfer to V-1201. Actual exposure and operating state require verification; extreme consequences are not established.

tickets.summary: The compression-module head failed two 50% LEL gas tests; the other two 2oo3 heads passed then, retaining hydrocarbon detection but leaving no margin for another head failure.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect gas path, optics, power and signal; have the instrument engineer disposition repair or replacement and recalibration. Check impairment/deviation register and controls. Bump-test head and verify 2oo3 response.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed head's required function is to respond to hydrocarbon test gas. It failed to respond on both attempts, confirming loss of that head's function; the other heads do not lower this likelihood.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this head degrades hydrocarbon gas detection in the compression module. The other two heads responded during the test, retaining the 2oo3 group's capability then, but leaving no margin for another head failure. Their present status is unverified.

tickets.summary: CR-5001's main hoist rope has 6 broken wires/lay at maximum boom radius versus a 10-wire discard limit, with poor lubrication. Hoist loss could injure personnel and halt supply-boat offloads, causing logistics problems within days.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect and lubricate the hoist rope; obtain lifting inspector disposition under the lifting standard, correct as directed, then recheck the 10-wire limit and hoisting performance. Survey full rope and all discard criteria. Check lift plans and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is the main hoist rope's ability to lift. Six broken wires per lay and poor lubrication show degradation, but the count remains below the stated 10-wire discard criterion. No loss of hoisting function or progression rate is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If the main hoist rope cannot lift, the crane has no listed redundancy and supply-boat offloads stop, creating a logistics problem within days. A rope failure during a lift also presents a credible personnel hazard; actual exposure is unverified.

tickets.summary: P-3305 has tripped three times this month, with wellhead-manifold inhibitor injection intermittent for around ten days. Production need not stop, but downstream carbon steel may corrode within weeks; diaphragm failure is suspected.
tickets.recommended_action: Have corrosion engineering assess under-injection and authorize fault-based repair. Retest stable manifold injection against the approved dosing criterion. Inspect diaphragm, discharge path and trip. Check current dosing and downstream steel.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The pump's required function is to deliver corrosion inhibitor to the wellhead manifold. Three low-discharge-pressure trips and logged intermittent injection establish repeated loss of that function; a diaphragm fault is only suspected.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of inhibitor delivery does not stop production immediately, but inhibitor starvation can initiate downstream carbon-steel corrosion within weeks, with delayed integrity consequences. No redundant pump is listed; the affected steel's condition is unknown.

tickets.summary: On 10 June, 12/60 north-quadrant nozzles failed spray delivery over two producing wellheads despite normal skid flow. A branch valve was reopened on 21 June after an unknown closure period, but deluge coverage remains unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect branch and nozzles; correct confirmed obstruction under fire-protection engineer disposition. Check nozzle impairment/deviation register. Witness full-flow retest of spray and coverage. Confirm obstruction cause and extent.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of effective deluge spray in the north quadrant. The full-flow test directly demonstrated loss of that function at approximately 12 nozzles; normal skid readings do not establish local delivery.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of local deluge coverage above two producing wellheads creates severe fire-protection exposure. Other nozzles delivered spray, but no capable alternative for the affected coverage is established; complete system loss is not claimed.

tickets.summary: On 11 June INST-2150 read ~12% above backup and ~15% above sight glass, worsening over three weeks while feeding V-1201 control and high-level alarm. A false level could misdirect both; backup was reported flatlined on 18 June, and current capability is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer: inspect both loops and impulse lines; correct findings and approve control/alarm disposition. Check impairment/deviation register. Compare both signals to sight glass and limits. Check control/alarm alignment and exposure. Test high-level alarm after correction.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The duty transmitter's indication has diverged progressively from the backup and sight glass for about three weeks while supplying control. impact_of_failure.rationale: If the duty level signal fails, it could misdirect V-1201 control and its high-level alarm. The backup was subsequently reported flatlined, so capable redundancy cannot be credited; present control, alarm and exposure conditions remain unverified.

tickets.summary: V-1305's inlet deflector is partly detached after one bracket corroded through; shell and heads were sound and the separator was out of service. Deflector failure could interrupt well testing, while bypass avoids production loss.
tickets.recommended_action: Have the integrity engineer approve repair of the deflector attachment before return; verify secure retention and inlet deflection to approved criteria after repair. Inspect all supports; confirm design criteria.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is secure inlet-flow deflection during well testing. A partly detached plate and corroded-through bracket are meaningful precursors, but loss of deflection is unverified. The separator was reported out of service, limiting near-term demand.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If inlet deflection fails during well testing, it could interrupt that service. The reported out-of-service state, sound shell and heads, and available isolation and bypass limit the supported consequence; production loss is not supported.

urgency.rationale: triage-policy-v5: ceil(0.7*I+0.3*L), L=5, I=4, base=5, final=5. These govern the approved repair and whether the separator can return to well-testing service; the inspection does not establish restored capability. Sources: finding:F-1014:finding_description, equipment:V-1305:engineer_comment.

tickets.summary: Dirty V-2450 gauge glass limits local level checks; transmitter control appears normal and no carryover is indicated. A missed level upset could expose turbines to damaging liquid carryover.
tickets.recommended_action: Clean and inspect gauge glass; restore readability. Refer any reading mismatch to an instrument engineer for disposition. Verify gauge readability and transmitter match.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is readable local level indication from the gauge glass. Dirt has degraded readability, but the finding does not establish that the level cannot be read; transmitter-based control appears normal.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of local indication would remove a level cross-check, while transmitter-based control appears normal and no downstream carryover is indicated. The scrubber protects turbines from damaging liquid carryover; that wider function is not shown to have failed.

urgency.rationale: triage-policy-v5: ceil(0.7*I+0.3*L), L=4, I=4, base=4, final=4. tickets.recommended_action: Inspect valve and tag; renew the corroded label once valve identity is established. Match installed valve to certificate/register; verify new tag legibility.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is PSV-3420 relieving compressor-discharge overpressure. impact_of_failure.rationale: If this valve failed to provide compressor-discharge overpressure protection, a non-redundant safety protection layer would be lost, with credible severe pressure-related consequences. The illegible tag does not reduce that hypothetical consequence.

tickets.summary: FW-8101 started, but 9.2 barg versus 11 design with flow unmeasured leaves firewater delivery uncertain; wear or a test-line valve is suspected. FW-8102 failed its first start on 3 June, then reached rated pressure; loss of both pumps would shut down production.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect test-line valve and pump; firewater engineer to set operating/repair disposition and correct confirmed faults. Check impairment/deviation register. Confirm criteria; measure FW-8101 pressure/flow now and after correction. Verify FW-8102 start and rated delivery.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: FW-8101 started and ran correctly, but discharge pressure stabilised at 9.2 barg against an 11 barg design value. This is a meaningful precursor to loss of required firewater delivery, not proof of that loss: flow was unmeasured, acceptance criteria are unstated, and a test-line valve remains a possible cause.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of FW-8101 firewater delivery could severely weaken fire protection. FW-8102 is the designated partner, but its earlier failed first start prevents crediting present readiness; its successful second start and rated discharge pressure do not establish simultaneous unavailability. The engineer states that both pumps being unavailable means production shutdown.

tickets.recommended_action: Investigate closure; fire engineer to direct valve disposition. Verify current protection control alignment. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Witness function test; close impairment only after pass. Check nozzle closeout and wellhead exposure. Trace valve closure and duration.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The chained-closed branch valve could not admit deluge water to the north quadrant when found. It was reopened immediately, but restored delivery was not demonstrated; the duration of closure is unknown.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of north-quadrant deluge delivery could leave producing wellheads without intended fire coverage. No redundant deluge arrangement is listed. Personnel exposure and the extent of any remaining coverage need checking; the consequence is not an observed fire.

tickets.summary: Wet, rust-stained insulation at the V-1201 manway may conceal shell or pipe corrosion. Vessel containment loss could release first-stage process fluid and expose personnel, but wall condition and leakage are unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Remove wet insulation; inspect exposed shell/pipe. Integrity engineer to assess service and direct any repair. Verify boundary integrity after correction. Check impairment/deviation register. Map shell/pipe UT against minima.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is containment by the V-1201 vessel pressure boundary. Damp, rust-stained insulation is a meaningful corrosion precursor, but the boundary is concealed and neither wall loss nor leakage is established. Its thick-walled, historically trouble-free construction limits what can be inferred about near-term loss.

impact_of_failure.rationale: If this vessel loses containment, a first-stage process release could expose personnel and interrupt production. It is the pressure boundary for the entire first stage, with no registered redundancy; the observed staining is not itself a release.
